Getting Started

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

typstR is built around one fast path: scaffold a working paper, edit one Quarto project, and render a PDF when Quarto is available.

Create a project

Start by creating a working paper directory:

library(typstR)
create_working_paper("my-paper")

This creates a small project with:

  • template.qmd for the manuscript
  • _quarto.yml for project settings
  • references.bib for bibliography entries
  • the bundled typstR extension used by the template

Know the three files you will edit most

The working-paper starter is intentionally small, and each file has a distinct job:

  • template.qmd is the manuscript you edit day to day
  • _quarto.yml stores project-level Quarto settings
  • references.bib is where you add bibliography entries

If you only remember one thing from this vignette, remember that the normal flow is template.qmd for content, _quarto.yml for project settings, and references.bib for citations.

Edit template.qmd

The working-paper template already contains the main fields most users need: title, authors, affiliations, an abstract, bibliography wiring, and a typstR: block for publication metadata.

typstR:
  keywords:
    - supply chains
    - trade policy
  jel:
    - F14
    - F13
  report-number: "WP 001"
  funding: |
    This research was supported by the Applied Trade Policy Programme.

You can also build structured metadata in R before pasting it into the Quarto file:

lead_author <- author(
  "Elena Fischer",
  email = "elena.fischer@example.org",
  corresponding = TRUE,
  affiliation = "1"
)

home_institute <- affiliation("1", "Centre for European Industrial Analysis")

metadata <- manuscript_meta(
  authors = list(lead_author),
  affiliations = list(home_institute)
)
yaml::as.yaml(metadata, handlers = list(logical = function(value) {
  structure(ifelse(value, "true", "false"), class = "verbatim")
}))
#> [1] "author:\n- name: Elena Fischer\n  affiliation: '1'\n  email: elena.fischer@example.org\n  corresponding: true\naffiliations:\n- id: '1'\n  name: Centre for European Industrial Analysis\n"

Use unquoted true and false for boolean settings. Values such as yes, no, on, off, numbers, and quoted boolean strings are rejected. The logical handler above avoids the YAML 1.1 yes/no output of yaml::as.yaml().

Check _quarto.yml and references.bib

The generated _quarto.yml keeps the project wiring minimal:

project:
  type: default

You usually do not need to change it on day one, but it is the place to look when you later want project-wide Quarto behavior.

The starter references.bib includes one example entry so you can see the expected BibTeX shape immediately. Add your own entries there and keep bibliography: references.bib in the manuscript YAML.

Add manuscript content

Keep the manuscript in template.qmd. The shipped starter uses a compact working-paper structure:

  • Introduction
  • Data and Methods
  • Results
  • Conclusion
  • References

Add citations through references.bib and cite them in the manuscript with standard Quarto syntax such as @smith2020.

Render the PDF

Rendering depends on Quarto, so the call below is shown but not run during vignette checks.

The minimum supported Quarto version is 1.4.11. Early Quarto 1.4 builds require a standalone Typst executable on PATH; the tested standalone version is 0.15.1. Newer Quarto builds include Typst. Use validate_render_environment() to check the compiler available to your selected Quarto installation.

render_working_paper("my-paper/template.qmd")

If you prefer to guard the call in your own scripts, use the same condition that package tests use:

quarto_ready <- quarto::quarto_available()
quarto_ready
#> [1] TRUE
if (quarto::quarto_available()) {
  render_working_paper("my-paper/template.qmd")
}

Validate before rendering 

validate_manuscript("my-paper/template.qmd")
validate_manuscript("my-paper", check_environment = TRUE)

The first call checks static YAML, publication metadata and configured files without requiring Quarto. Rendering runs those same checks plus Quarto/Typst and extension checks automatically. validate_render_environment() remains an environment-only check. Errors include stable diagnostic codes, locations and repair hints.

Every variant needs a text title and the bundled typstR-typst format. Select workingpaper (default), article or brief with typstR: format-variant. Authors, affiliations, abstract, keywords, JEL codes, report numbers and branding are optional; supplied fields must have the documented types. Omit unused optional fields; Quarto rejects null for typed fields such as abstract and bibliography. Change inherited settings using a valid value or edit the declaring configuration. Literal citation examples inside fenced/inline code do not require a bibliography; citations in prose or the abstract do. Inline reference records need unique text IDs.

File input works from outside the project, including paths with spaces. Directory input selects one immediate .qmd; NULL searches the current directory and reports ambiguity rather than guessing. The nearest _quarto.yml establishes the project root. Project settings, directory _metadata.yml and manuscript YAML are merged. Local resources (bibliography, logo, CSL and include files) resolve relative to the YAML file that declares them. Configured files must already exist.

Static preflight rejects profiles, publication overrides in either _quarto.yml.local or _quarto.yaml.local, metadata-files, executable YAML and remote resources. It does not evaluate code-generated resources/citations or validate the whole Quarto schema. Empty/editor-only local files are allowed; move publication settings into the main project or document YAML for static validation. Conflicting overrides are reported with their file path. Citeproc checks bibliography contents at render time. For unsupported configuration, use Quarto directly and verify the output.

Layout and existing projects

Section numbering is enabled by default. Set number-sections: false to disable it; toc: true adds a contents list after the abstract, with toc-title and toc-depth controlling its title and depth. papersize: a4 selects A4 paper. Render helpers honor output-file and project output-dir when opening PDFs.

Scaffolds contain their own extension copy. Updating the R package does not change existing projects. Back up _extensions/typstR/, then replace that directory with the contents of system.file("quarto/extensions/typstR", package = "typstR"). Keep your manuscript, bibliography, and project configuration; only replace the extension.

In an output: asis R chunk, appendix_title("Additional Data") starts lettered appendices in working papers and articles. Subsequent appendix headings at the same level use B, C, and so on; nested headings use A.1, A.2, and so on. Briefs retain ordinary numbering. Disabling section numbering disables appendix numbering as well.
